mainTopic: How long a court announces a sale of orphans' or הקדש property, and when it may sell young orphans' property to pay a debt or a כתובה.
overview: A ברייתא gives three opinions on how long a court must announce a sale of orphans' property and of הקדש property. רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, rules sixty days for orphans and says this follows רבי מאיר. He explains that רבי מאיר's thirty days means announcing every day, while sixty days means announcing only on Mondays and Thursdays. The גמרא then brings a dispute about when the court may sell young orphans' property to pay a debt at all. רב אסי says only when interest is eating into it. רבי יוחנן adds a widow's כתובה, because her food support keeps costing the estate. A משנה, a משנה in גיטין, and a ברייתא are each brought as challenges, and the answers end with the idea that these cases are about a father who admitted he still owed. A story about a divorced woman's כתובה shows another version of רבי יוחנן's reason: חינא, so that she can remarry. Finally, רב נחמן explains why he began collecting from orphans, and the הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: we hold back only when there is a doubt whether the father already paid.

steps.title: Three opinions on how long to announce a sale
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a three-way argument about how many days to announce the sale of orphans' property and of הקדש property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Orphans' property is announced for thirty days and consecrated property for sixty days, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: orphans' property for sixty days, consecrated property for ninety days. The חכמים say: both are announced for sixty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three opinions on how long the court announces a sale before selling orphans' property or consecrated property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees there must be a public announcement period before the sale. They argue only about its length. רבי מאיר says 30 for orphans and 60 for הקדש, רבי יהודה says 60 and 90, and the חכמים say 60 for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Appraisal; the court's valuing and public offering of property for sale
Orphans, here minors whose inherited property is being sold

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the numbers straight: 'sixty days for orphans' is רבי יהודה's view and also the חכמים' view, but not רבי מאיר's. The rest of the discussion depends on this.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The appraisal of the orphans' property is announced for thirty days,
and the appraisal of consecrated property is announced for sixty days,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The appraisal of the orphans' property is for sixty days,
and the appraisal of consecrated property is for ninety days.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: Both this and that are for sixty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of how long the announcement period lasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: orphans 30, הקדש 60. רבי יהודה: orphans 60, הקדש 90. חכמים: both 60.

steps.title: The ruling: orphans' property is announced for sixty days
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, rules that the הלכה is sixty days for orphans' property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: The הלכה is that orphans' property is announced for sixty days.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the practical ruling: orphans' property is announced for sixty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sixty days for orphans matches both רבי יהודה and the חכמים. The ruling does not say whose opinion it follows, and the next steps make that question the center of the discussion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the statement that the rest of the passage questions and then defends.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says that Avimi says:
The halakha is that the appraisal of the orphans' property is announced for sixty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the הלכה on one part of the ברייתא's argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is sixty days of announcement for orphans' property.

steps.title: Did you say sixty or thirty?
steps.stepSummary: While רבי חייא בר אבין repeats the ruling, רב נחמן בר יצחק asks him to confirm the number. He answers: sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין was sitting and saying this teaching. רב נחמן בר יצחק asked him: Did you say sixty or thirty? He answered: Sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רב נחמן בר יצחק checks the exact number in the ruling, and this sets up a series of questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both numbers appear in the ברייתא, so it is easy to mix them up. Confirming 'sixty' is the first step in pinning down exactly what the ruling says.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin was sitting
and saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: This means the ruling of רב חסדא in the name of אבימי from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said
to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin:
Did you say sixty, or did you say thirty?
He said to him: Sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשִּׁים קָאָמְרַתְּ אוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts checking the details of the ruling from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was the number sixty or thirty?

steps.title: Orphans' property or consecrated property?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks whether the sixty days refers to orphans' or consecrated property. The answer is orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it about orphans' property or consecrated property? He answered: Orphans' property.
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner keeps narrowing down the ruling and now confirms which kind of property it covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Sixty days' fits two different cases in the ברייתא: הקדש according to רבי מאיר, and orphans according to רבי יהודה and the חכמים. Knowing it is about orphans tells us which opinions the ruling could match.

phrases.english: Of orphans, or of consecrated property?
He said to him: Of orphans.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּיתוֹמִים אוֹ דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the step-by-step check.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which property does the sixty days apply to?

steps.title: Whose opinion does the ruling follow?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks whether the ruling follows רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה. The answer is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it like רבי מאיר or like רבי יהודה? He answered: Like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The last clarifying question asks which תנא the ruling follows. The answer sets up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We would expect the answer to be רבי יהודה, since he says sixty for orphans. The answer 'רבי מאיר' is surprising, and the challenge comes right after.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Meir, or in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?
He said to him: In accordance with Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the clarifications and leads into the challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא does the ruling follow?

steps.title: But רבי מאיר said thirty!
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects that רבי מאיר said thirty days for orphans, not sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי מאיר says thirty!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner points out a contradiction: the ruling says sixty and claims to follow רבי מאיר, but רבי מאיר said thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא (step 1), רבי מאיר says orphans' property is announced for thirty days. A sixty-day ruling therefore cannot simply follow רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Meir says thirty!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a sixty-day ruling for orphans follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says רבי מאיר holds thirty days for orphans, which contradicts sixty.

steps.title: Thirty days means announcing on consecutive days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין reports that רב חסדא raised this same question to אבימי and was rebuked for it. אבימי explained that רבי מאיר's thirty days applies when the announcing is done every day in a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב חסדא said: I took many blows from אבימי over this teaching. If the court comes to announce on consecutive days, it is thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. רבי מאיר's 'thirty days' refers to announcing every day in a row, so sixty days can also fit his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer shows the two numbers are not really in conflict. They describe different ways of announcing. Thirty is for daily, back-to-back announcing, while sixty is for a spread-out schedule. רב חסדא adds that he was harshly rebuked when he asked אבימי this same question.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, orphans' property is announced for thirty days if the announcing is done every day in a row. That is why a sixty-day ruling can still be said to follow רבי מאיר.
steps.confusionAlert: The thirty and sixty days are not two opposing rulings. They describe the same requirement carried out in two different ways, daily or spread out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Ḥisda said:
From Avimi I absorbed many blows
phrases.notes: רב חסדא means אבימי scolded him harshly when he raised this same question.

phrases.english: over this teaching;
if he comes to announce on consecutive days, it is thirty.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different announcement schedules lead to different numbers of days.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's thirty days seemed to contradict a sixty-day ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's thirty days applies to consecutive daily announcing, so sixty can fit his view under a different schedule.

steps.title: Monday and Thursday announcing takes sixty days
steps.stepSummary: אבימי finishes his answer. Announcing only on שני וחמישי takes sixty days. There are only about eighteen real announcing days, but because the process is spread out, people hear about the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you announce only on Mondays and Thursdays, it takes sixty days. True, if you count the actual announcing days, there are only eighteen. But since the whole thing stretches out over a long time, people hear about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אבימי's answer from the previous step. Thirty days is for daily announcing; sixty days is for announcing only on Mondays and Thursdays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the contradiction with רבי מאיר: there are two different ways of announcing, so there are two different time periods. The גמרא admits that sixty days of Monday and Thursday announcing gives fewer actual announcements, about eighteen, than thirty straight days. It says this is still enough, because a long stretch of time also helps word spread.

keyTerms.meaning: Monday and Thursday, the regular days when people gathered in town
the matter stretches out over time

steps.whatToRemember: Thirty days means announcing every day. Sixty days means announcing only on שני וחמישי. Both fit רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: On Monday and Thursday: sixty.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ מָר
phrases.english: And even though when the master counts them,
phrases.notes: "Master" is a polite way of saying "you" here.

phrases.english: the days of announcing
come to only eighteen days,
since the matter stretches out,
people hear about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֵׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי, שִׁשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אבימי's answer, which began in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: two different ways of announcing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sixty days contradicts רבי מאיר's thirty days for orphans.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thirty days is for daily announcing. Sixty days is for שני וחמישי announcing, which still lets people hear because it lasts longer.

steps.title: When the court sells orphans' property to pay a debt
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the court steps in for orphans' property only when interest is eating into it. רבי יוחנן adds a second case: a widow's כתובה, because of her ongoing food support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: the court does not get involved with orphans' property unless interest is eating it up. רבי יוחנן says: either for a loan document with interest, or for a wife's כתובה, because of food support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: when will the court sell young orphans' property to pay their father's debts? Two אמוראים give their rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the court waits until the orphans grow up. רב אסי allows an early sale only when interest is growing the debt and hurting the orphans. רבי יוחנן agrees, and adds the widow's כתובה. Until she is paid, the estate keeps paying for her food, so paying her now saves the orphans money.

keyTerms.meaning: the court steps in and deals with it, here by selling property to pay a debt
the money a wife is owed from her husband's estate
food support owed to the widow

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the section. The two rules are now tested against each other and against the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav Asi:
We do not deal with orphans' property,
phrases.notes: He means the court won't sell the orphans' property to pay a debt now; it waits until they grow up.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה רִבִּית אוֹכֶלֶת בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: unless interest was eating into it.
And Rabbi Yochanan says:
either for a loan document that carries interest,
or for a wife's marriage contract, because of food support.
phrases.notes: Until the widow is paid, the orphans must keep feeding her from the estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: אֵין נִזְקָקִין לְנִכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about selling orphans' property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רב אסי, the court sells orphans' property early only when interest is growing the debt. Per רבי יוחנן, also for a widow's כתובה, because of her food support.

steps.title: Why רב אסי leaves out the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב אסי did not include the widow's כתובה. It answers that the Rabbis gave the estate her earnings, which balance out her food costs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי, why didn't he say the court steps in for a wife's כתובה? Because the Rabbis set it up that her handiwork goes to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב אסי disagrees with רבי יוחנן about the כתובה, and then gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אסי, the widow's food is not a real loss to the orphans. The Rabbis arranged that her earnings go to the estate, and those earnings pay for her food. With no loss, there is no reason to sell early.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi, what is the reason
he did not say "for a wife's marriage contract"?

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ,
phrases.english: Because the Rabbis enacted for him her handiwork.
phrases.notes: Her earnings go to the estate, which makes up for the cost of feeding her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַסִּי מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר לִכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב אסי does not include רבי יוחנן's second case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב אסי does not count the כתובה as a reason to sell early.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her earnings (מעשה ידיה) go to the estate, so feeding her costs the orphans nothing.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן still includes the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן answers that point. Sometimes her earnings do not cover the cost of her food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Sometimes it is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוחנן: given that the estate gets her earnings, why does he still sell early? It answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן accepts that the estate gets her earnings. He points out that they do not always cover her food, so the orphans can still lose money. That possible loss is enough reason to pay her כתובה now.

keyTerms.meaning: the other one, the other opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument over the כתובה is one question: does her work always pay for her food? רב אסי says yes, so there is no loss. רבי יוחנן says not always, so the court steps in.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רבי יוחנן: why does he still count the כתובה?

phrases.english: Sometimes it is not enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? זִימְנִין דְּלָא סָפְקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the flip side of step 10, from רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוחנן deals with the fact that the estate gets her earnings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her earnings sometimes do not cover her food, so the orphans can still lose.

steps.title: The משנה seems to sell even with no interest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about announcing orphans' property for thirty days. It shows the creditor must be Jewish, and a Jew may not collect interest. So the משנה must be a case with no interest, yet the court still sells.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: the appraisal of orphans' property is announced for thirty days, and of הקדש for sixty days, morning and evening. What case is this? If a non-Jewish creditor, would he obey? So it must be a Jewish creditor. If he is collecting interest, would we allow that? So it must be a case without interest, and still the משנה says the court steps in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי and רבי יוחנן from our משנה. It narrows down the case in the משנה step by step until it reaches one with no interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא rules out options one at a time. A non-Jewish creditor would not wait thirty days for a Jewish court. A Jewish creditor may not take interest from a Jew, and the court would not allow it. That leaves a debt with no interest, and the משנה still has the court selling. This goes against both אמוראים, who need interest or a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: appraisal, valuing property before selling it
what case are we dealing with?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אמוראים have been proven wrong. רבי יוחנן's answer comes in step 13, and רב אסי's answer comes in step 19.

phrases.english: We learned: the appraisal of orphans' property is thirty days,
and the appraisal of consecrated property is sixty days,
and we announce in the morning and in the evening.
What case are we dealing with?
If you say a non-Jewish creditor,
would he obey?
phrases.notes: He won't agree to wait thirty days just because a Jewish court says so.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously a Jewish creditor.
If he is collecting interest,
would we let him?
phrases.notes: A Jew may not take interest from a Jew, so the court would never allow it.

phrases.english: So rather, where he is not collecting interest,
and still it teaches: "we deal with it"!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rules from step 9 against our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב אסי and רבי יוחנן that the court sells orphans' property only for interest (or a כתובה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling out the other options leaves only a Jewish creditor with no interest, and the משנה still has the court selling.

steps.title: The משנה fits רבי יוחנן but seems to contradict רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: The no-interest case in the משנה fits רבי יוחנן, who can explain it as a widow's כתובה. It is a problem for רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי יוחנן, because he can say the משנה is about a wife's כתובה. But for רב אסי it is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 12. The משנה works for רבי יוחנן but is hard for רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed the משנה must be a case where no interest is eating the estate. רבי יוחנן allows the court to sell for a widow's כתובה too, so he can place the משנה there. רב אסי allows a sale only when interest is involved, so the משנה seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well for (this opinion), setting up a contrast with the other opinion
He sets it up as, meaning he explains which case the source is talking about
The payment a wife receives from her husband's estate when he dies
It is a difficulty, a challenge that needs an answer

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yochanan,
he can set it up as a case of a wife's כתובה,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה about announcing orphans' property for thirty days, from step 12.

phrases.english: but according to Rav Asi it is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה, אֶלָּא לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 12 by spelling out whom it hurts
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that the court acts for orphans only when interest is involved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has the court selling with no interest, which only רבי יוחנן's widow's כתובה case can explain

steps.title: רב אסי answers that רבי יוחנן has a problem too
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי argues the משנה does not fit רבי יוחנן either. Why wait thirty days to announce, losing food money for sure, for a sale that may not bring any gain?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי can tell you: Does it really work for רבי יוחנן? Would we give up on the food support, which is surely costing the estate, and choose a long announcement when we don't even know if it will bring a better price?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי pushes back. The משנה is hard for רבי יוחנן too, so it is no special proof against רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason for selling for the widow is that her daily food support keeps draining the estate. If so, the court should sell quickly. Spending thirty days announcing means a sure loss on food, all for a possible gain that may never come.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it work out well? A way of saying the other side has a problem too
Food support the estate must give the widow
The public announcement of the property before a court sale

phrases.english: Rav Asi can say to you:
And according to Rabbi Yochanan, does it work out well?
Do we leave aside the food support
which is certainly causing a loss,
phrases.notes: Every day of the thirty, the orphans keep paying for the widow's food.

phrases.english: and choose the announcement
about which we don't know if we will gain
or will not gain?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב אַסִּי: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects step 13's challenge by showing the opposing view faces a similar problem
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the משנה supports רבי יוחנן over רב אסי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי יוחנן's reason (food costs), a thirty-day delay makes no sense

steps.title: The widow claimed her כתובה in court, so her food support stopped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's side answers that the משנה is about a widow who claimed her כתובה in court. Following רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, she no longer gets food support, so the delay costs nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not a problem. The case is a widow who claims her כתובה in court. As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a woman who claims her כתובה in court no longer gets food support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. In the משנה's case the widow's food support has already stopped, so waiting thirty days loses nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's attack depended on the food costs continuing during the announcement. According to שמואל, once a widow goes to court to collect her כתובה, she gives up her food support. So the court can announce slowly and still look for a better price.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not a difficulty, opening an answer
She claims payment of her כתובה
Food support from the husband's estate

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
it is where she claims her כתובה in court,
in line with what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,
for Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who claims her כתובה in court
has no food support.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, בְּתוֹבַעַת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's counter-challenge in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) using an outside ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The widow's food support keeps running during the thirty days of announcing
steps.terutzMaskana: She claimed her כתובה in court, so her food support has ended and the delay costs nothing

steps.title: If the orphans lose nothing, why should the court act at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the widow's food support has stopped, the orphans lose nothing by waiting. So the court should not handle her claim at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should not deal with her case at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If there is no loss to the orphans, why sell their property now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's whole reason for selling orphans' property for a widow was to stop a loss. Once her food support has ended, that loss is gone. So the court should wait until the orphans grow up.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, used to draw out a problem from what was just said
We (the court) attend to, meaning take up and handle the case

phrases.english: If so,
we should not attend to her at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אִיזְדְּקוֹקֵי לָא מִיזְדַּקְקִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the widow claimed her כתובה in court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without food costs there is no loss to the orphans, so there is no reason for the court to step in

steps.title: Once the court started her case, it finishes it
steps.stepSummary: Since the court took up her claim at the start, it continues and finishes the collection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since we dealt with her at the start, we deal with her until the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that once the court got involved, it sees the case through to the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she first came to collect, she was still receiving food support, so the court had a good reason to get involved. Having started, it does not drop the case just because that reason has now gone away.

phrases.english: Rather, since we attended to her at the start,
we attend to her at the end too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּאִיזְדַּקְקִינַן לַהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא, מִיזְדַּקְקִינַן לַהּ לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Procedural principle: a case the court has started, it finishes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With no ongoing loss, the court should not handle the widow's claim
steps.terutzMaskana: The court's original involvement was justified, so it carries the case through to the end

steps.title: Back to the problem for רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: Whatever happens with רבי יוחנן, the משנה is still a difficulty for רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is still difficult for רב אסי!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי יוחנן's side is settled, the גמרא goes back to the original challenge. רב אסי still has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's counterattack in step 14 was answered, so he can no longer say both sides have the same problem. The challenge from steps 12 and 13 stands again: a Jewish creditor cannot charge interest, so how can the משנה be an interest case?

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, returning to the main point

phrases.english: In any case,
for Rav Asi it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge of step 13 after the side discussion about רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that only interest justifies the court selling orphans' property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה must be a case with no interest, since a Jewish creditor cannot charge interest

steps.title: A non-Jewish creditor who accepted Jewish law
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a non-Jewish creditor, who may charge interest. He accepted Jewish law, so he waits the thirty days of announcing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is a non-Jewish creditor who agreed to be judged by Jewish law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב אסי. The משנה is an interest case after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed the creditor in the משנה must be Jewish, because a non-Jew would not wait thirty days. But a non-Jewish creditor who agreed to Jewish law will wait, and he may still charge interest. So interest is eating into the estate, and רב אסי's rule fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Really or actually, keeping an earlier idea and adding a detail

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions can explain the משנה. For רבי יוחנן, it is a widow who claimed her כתובה in court and so no longer receives food support. For רב אסי, it is a non-Jewish creditor charging interest who agreed to follow Jewish law and wait thirty days.
steps.confusionAlert: The creditor is allowed to charge interest here because he is a non-Jew, not because of anything he chose. His accepting Jewish law only explains why he agrees to wait the thirty days.

phrases.english: Actually, it is a non-Jewish creditor,
who accepted upon himself
to be judged by Jewish law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי, שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed challenge to רב אסי in step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A non-Jewish creditor would never wait thirty days, so the creditor must be Jewish and cannot charge interest
steps.terutzMaskana: A non-Jewish creditor who accepted Jewish law waits thirty days and still charges interest, so the משנה fits רב אסי

steps.title: If He Accepted Jewish Law, Why Does He Still Take Interest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the non-Jewish creditor answer. If he follows Jewish law by waiting thirty days, he should also follow Jewish law and stop taking interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also not take interest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 19. If the non-Jewish creditor accepted Jewish law, he should also give up the interest that Jewish law forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the non-Jewish creditor waits the thirty days of announcing because he accepted Jewish law. But Jewish law also forbids taking ריבית. So accepting Jewish law should cancel the interest, and then there would be no loss to the orphans that requires the court to act.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the case

phrases.english: If so,
he should also not take interest!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רִבִּית נָמֵי לָא לִישְׁקוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 19 about the non-Jewish creditor who accepted Jewish law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the non-Jewish creditor accepted Jewish law and so waits thirty days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accepting Jewish law should be all-or-nothing. If he accepted it, he should also stop charging interest, and then the court would have no reason to act for the orphans.

steps.title: He Accepted Only the Thirty-Day Wait
steps.stepSummary: He accepted Jewish law for one matter, the waiting period, but not for the other, the interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He accepted it upon himself for this, but did not accept it upon himself for that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that his acceptance of Jewish law was partial. He agreed to wait the thirty days but did not agree to give up interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Acceptance does not have to cover everything. The creditor took on only the thirty-day announcement period. Interest still builds up, so the court has a reason to step in for the orphans, and the משנה still fits רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted upon himself (agreed to follow)
For this one... for that one

phrases.english: That he accepted upon himself for this,
phrases.notes: "This" is the thirty-day period of announcing the sale.

phrases.english: but did not accept upon himself for that.
phrases.notes: "That" is giving up the interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the acceptance was partial.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting Jewish law means accepting all of it, including the ban on interest.
steps.terutzMaskana: He accepted only the thirty-day wait. Interest keeps building, so the court acts, and the answer for רב אסי holds.

steps.title: Challenge From the Rule of Collecting From Orphans' Poorest Land
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in גיטין says creditors collect from orphans only from the poorest land. That has to mean a Jewish creditor who charges no interest, and yet the court acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'We collect from orphans' property only from the poorest land.' What case are we dealing with? If you say a non-Jewish creditor, would he agree to that? So it must be a Jewish creditor. If interest were building up, would we let him? So no interest is building up, and still it teaches that the court acts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to show the court acts on orphans' property even when no interest is building up. That goes against רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא narrows the case in the משנה in two moves. First, a non-Jewish creditor would never accept the worst land, so it must be a Jewish creditor. Second, a Jewish creditor is not allowed to take interest, so no interest is building up. Even so, the משנה describes the court collecting from the orphans, which means the court does act (נזקקין) without any interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Would he listen? Would he agree?
The court steps in and acts (here, on orphans' property)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"We do not collect from orphans' property
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in גיטין 48b.

phrases.english: except from the poorest land."
What case are we dealing with?
If you say with a non-Jewish creditor —
would he agree?
phrases.notes: A non-Jewish creditor would not accept being paid with the worst land.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously with a Jewish creditor.
If interest is eating away —
phrases.notes: Literally "interest is eating": the debt keeps growing and eats into the orphans' property.

phrases.english: would we let him?
Rather, it is where interest is not eating away,
and it teaches: the court acts!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין נִפְרָעִין מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים אֶלָּא מִן הַזִּיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from a different משנה, now that the first משנה has been settled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rules of רב אסי and רבי יוחנן (step 9) that the court acts on orphans' property only when interest is building up (or, for רבי יוחנן, also for a widow's כתובה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Narrowing the case: a non-Jew would not accept the worst land, and a Jew may not take interest. So the משנה describes collecting from orphans without interest, which shows the court does act.

steps.title: Fine for רבי יוחנן, a Problem for רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן can read the משנה as speaking about a wife's כתובה, but רב אסי has no such way out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted for רבי יוחנן, he sets it in the case of a wife's כתובה. But for רב אסי it is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sorts out who is really hurt by the challenge in Step 22. רבי יוחנן is safe, and רב אסי is left with the difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן already holds that the court acts for a widow's כתובה. So he can say the משנה about the poorest land is talking about a כתובה. רב אסי allows the court to act only when interest is building up, so the משנה contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it in (explains it as speaking about) a specific case

phrases.english: Granted, according to רבי יוחנן,
he sets it in the case of a wife's כתובה,
but according to רב אסי it is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה, אֶלָּא לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens Step 22, aiming the challenge at רב אסי alone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only רבי יוחנן can explain the משנה as a כתובה case. רב אסי is left facing a ruling where the court acts without interest.

steps.title: רב אסי Fires Back: רבי יוחנן's Reading Has a Problem Too
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי argues that if the משנה is about a כתובה, there is no reason to mention orphans. A כתובה is paid from the poorest land even when the husband himself pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי can say to you: And does it work well for רבי יוחנן? If it is a כתובה, why mention orphans specifically? Even from the husband himself, it is also paid from the poorest land!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers by challenging the other side. He argues that the כתובה reading does not fit the משנה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי assumes a כתובה is always paid from the poorest land, even by a living husband. If so, the משנה's rule about orphans adds nothing new for a כתובה. That suggests the משנה is not about a כתובה, and then רבי יוחנן has no better explanation than רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (this is how he would respond)

phrases.english: רב אסי can say to you:
And according to רבי יוחנן, does it work well?
If it is a כתובה,
why specifically from orphans?
Even from him himself,
phrases.notes: He means the husband paying during his lifetime, as in a divorce.

phrases.english: it is also from the poorest land!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב אַסִּי: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by attacking רבי יוחנן's way of reading the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of the משנה as a wife's כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a כתובה is always paid from the poorest land, the משנה's focus on orphans would be pointless. So the כתובה reading does not fit the wording.

steps.title: The משנה Follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי מאיר. He holds a כתובה is normally paid from middle-quality land, and from orphans only from the poorest land, so mentioning orphans is meaningful.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. It is רבי מאיר, who says: a wife's כתובה is paid from middle-quality land, and from orphans from the poorest land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. It says the משנה follows רבי מאיר, for whom orphans really are a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's challenge assumed a כתובה is always paid from the poorest land. רבי מאיר disagrees: normally it comes from middle land (בינונית), and only when collected from orphans does it drop to the poorest land (זיבורית). So the משנה's mention of orphans teaches something new, and רבי יוחנן's כתובה reading works.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads the משנה about orphans' poorest land as a כתובה case following רבי מאיר, where orphans pay less well than the husband would. That leaves רב אסי as the one still facing the challenge from this משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: There are three land levels: best (עידית), middle (בינונית), and poorest (זיבורית). רבי מאיר does not say a כתובה is always from the poorest land. That happens only when it is collected from orphans.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
it is רבי מאיר,
who says: a wife's כתובה is from middle-quality land,
and from orphans, from the poorest land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's challenge in Step 24 and saves רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a particular תנא (רבי מאיר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כתובה is always paid from the poorest land, so mentioning orphans would add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, a כתובה is normally paid from middle land and from orphans only from the poorest land, so the משנה's mention of orphans is meaningful.

steps.title: The גיטין משנה still challenges רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: Even after explaining why the משנה mentions orphans, the גמרא says the משנה is still a problem for רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, the משנה is still a difficulty for רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main question. Even if the משנה follows רבי מאיר, it still shows the court selling orphans' land for a creditor, and that is hard for רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 only explained why orphans are mentioned in the כתובה case. It did not solve the creditor part of the משנה. A Jewish creditor charges no interest, so by רב אסי's view the court should not get involved, yet the משנה says it does.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult for רב אסי!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side point about רבי מאיר is settled, the גמרא goes back to the original challenge from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's view that the court gets involved with orphans' property only when interest is growing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has the court collecting from orphans for a creditor, and a Jewish creditor does not charge interest.

steps.title: A non-Jewish creditor who accepted Jewish law
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a non-Jewish creditor who agreed to be judged by Jewish law, so he accepts the poorest land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה is talking about a non-Jewish creditor who agreed to be judged by Jewish law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. The creditor in the משנה is a non-Jew, so interest is involved, and he agreed to follow Jewish law, so he takes the poorest land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This solves both parts of the problem. Because he is a non-Jew, interest is growing, so even רב אסי agrees the court acts. Because he accepted Jewish law, the rule of collecting from the poorest land applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (used to start a defense)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same answer the גמרא gave earlier (step 19). It is not repeated by accident. Here it is being used again to explain a new source, the משנה in גיטין.

phrases.english: Actually, it is about a non-Jewish creditor,
who agreed to be judged by Jewish law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26 by changing who the creditor is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The creditor in the משנה is Jewish, so there is no interest.
steps.terutzMaskana: The creditor is a non-Jew who charges interest but agreed to Jewish rules of collection.

steps.title: Then he should not charge interest either
steps.stepSummary: If he accepted Jewish law, he should also give up interest, which Jewish law forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also not take interest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If this non-Jew follows Jewish law, he should follow it all the way and stop charging interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 27 needed two things at once: he follows Jewish law, and he still charges interest. The challenge is that these seem to clash. If interest stops, רב אסי's reason for the court to get involved is gone.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, רִבִּית נָמֵי לָא נִישְׁקוֹל!
phrases.english: If so, let him also not take interest!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רִבִּית נָמֵי לָא נִישְׁקוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the creditor accepted Jewish law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Jewish law forbids interest, so a creditor who accepted it should not collect interest, and then רב אסי has no reason for the court to act.

steps.title: He accepted one rule but not the other
steps.stepSummary: He accepted Jewish law about how to collect, but not about giving up interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He accepted it for this matter, but did not accept it for that matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the non-Jew picked and chose. He agreed to the Jewish rules of collection but kept charging interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting Jewish law does not have to be all or nothing. Because interest is still growing, רב אסי agrees the court should step in. So the משנה in גיטין fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: For this matter... for that matter

phrases.english: He accepted it for this matter,
phrases.notes: This means the rules about collecting the debt.

phrases.english: but he did not accept it for that matter.
phrases.notes: This means giving up interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁקִּיבֵּל לְזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: partial acceptance of Jewish law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting Jewish law means accepting all of it, including no interest.
steps.terutzMaskana: He accepted the collection rules only, so interest still grows and the court acts.

steps.title: A ברייתא about selling orphans' land for a כתובה or a debt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying orphans' land is sold to pay a wife's כתובה or a creditor's debt. The creditor part is easy for both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'in order to give the wife her כתובה and the creditor his debt.' The creditor part is fine for both רב אסי and רבי יוחנן, as we explained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source and starts setting up a challenge. First it says the creditor part is no problem for anyone; the real problem is coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creditor part can be explained the same way as before: a non-Jewish creditor who charges interest. So it does not hurt רב אסי or רבי יוחנן. This clears the way to focus on the כתובה part.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to; on condition that
The money a husband owes his wife by marriage contract
Both according to this sage and that sage

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'In order to give the wife her כתובה
and the creditor his debt.'
Granted, the creditor part:
for both this sage and that sage, it is as we answered.
phrases.notes: The two sages are רב אסי and רבי יוחנן. 'As we answered' means the non-Jewish creditor who charges interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַל מְנָת לִיתֵּן לָאִשָּׁה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה is settled, a new source is brought against רב אסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the challenge: the creditor clause is explained as before, leaving the כתובה clause to be examined.

steps.title: The כתובה part is hard for רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: Selling orphans' land for a כתובה fits רבי יוחנן but not רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the כתובה part: for רבי יוחנן it works, but for רב אסי it is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the real challenge comes. The ברייתא lets the court sell orphans' land to pay a כתובה, which רבי יוחנן allows but רב אסי does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כתובה has no interest, so the 'non-Jewish creditor' answer does not help here. רבי יוחנן includes the כתובה among the cases where the court acts, so he has no problem. רב אסי does not, so the ברייתא seems to argue against him.

phrases.english: But her כתובה:
granted, according to רבי יוחנן it works out,
but according to רב אסי it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּתוּבָּתָהּ, בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge started in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's view that the court does not act on orphans' property for a כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says orphans' land is sold to pay a כתובה, and no interest is involved there.

steps.title: The father admitted he still owed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a case where the father admitted before he died that he had not paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? When the one who owes admits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי by narrowing the case. The father admitted the debt was still unpaid, so the court can collect from the orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the court holds back with orphans because maybe the father already paid and they cannot argue for themselves. Here the father himself admitted he still owed, so that worry is gone. So even רב אסי agrees the court sells the land.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrow case)
The one who owes admits the debt

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
When the one who owes admits it.
phrases.notes: The one who owes is the father, who admitted before he died that he had not yet paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about any כתובה owed from orphans' property.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a case where the father admitted the debt, so the court collects without holding back.

steps.title: The admission answer explains every case
steps.stepSummary: Now that we have the 'he admitted' answer, all the earlier sources can be explained that way too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, all of them are also when the one who owes admits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up. The answer 'the one who owes admitted' works for all the sources, so we do not need the non-Jewish creditor idea anymore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the creditor cases needed the idea of a non-Jew who charges interest. Now even a Jewish creditor works, because the father admitted the debt. One simple answer covers every source, and none of them goes against רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this answer

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי holds the court gets involved with orphans' property only when interest is growing. Sources that seem to disagree are explained as cases where the father admitted he still owed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא choosing one simple answer that fits everything, instead of a separate answer for each source.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
all of them are also when the one who owes admits it.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the earlier creditor cases too, so the creditor can be Jewish.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 32 and uses it for all the earlier sources.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every source that seemed to argue against רב אסי is about a case where the father admitted the debt. So there is no need for the non-Jewish creditor explanation.

steps.title: A divorced woman collects her כתובה from orphans' property
steps.stepSummary: מרימר collected a כתובה for a divorced woman from the property of orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר collected a marriage contract payment for a divorced woman from the property of orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a ruling in a real case. This story sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father had divorced his wife and died before paying her כתובה. מרימר let her collect right away from the orphans' property, even though they are still young. This seems to go against רב אסי's rule from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Mareimar collected
phrases.notes: Watch the names: the story starts with מרימר, but in the next line רבינא speaks to אמימר, as the text is printed here.

phrases.english: a marriage contract for a divorced woman
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'her כתובה' (round brackets); the corrected wording, in square brackets, just says 'a כתובה'.

phrases.english: from the property of orphans.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר אַגְבֵּי כְּתוּבָּה לִגְרוּשָׁה מִנִּכְסֵי דְּיַתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier sources are settled, the גמרא brings a story of an actual ruling about orphans' property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A divorced woman was allowed to collect her כתובה from young orphans' property.

steps.title: רבינא objects using רב אסי and רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks: רב אסי says we only touch orphans' property when interest is eating it up, and רבי יוחנן only adds a note with interest or a wife's כתובה because of food support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to אמימר: But רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: 'We do not deal with orphans' property unless interest is eating it up.' רבי יוחנן says: 'Also for a loan note that has interest, or for a wife's כתובה, because of her food support.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the ruling of the story. He quotes the two opinions about when a court may touch orphans' property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב אסי, a court only acts when interest is growing against the orphans, and that is not the case here. By רבי יוחנן, a court acts for a wife's כתובה, but his reason is מזוני: her daily food costs the orphans money. A divorced woman gets no food support, so the reason does not seem to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: the court deals with, gets involved with
interest that is 'eating up' the property
food support (that a widow gets from the estate)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Ameimar:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav Asi:
"We do not deal with the property of orphans

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה רִבִּית אוֹכֶלֶת בָּהֶן״.
phrases.english: unless interest was eating it up."
Rabbi Yochanan says:
Either for a loan note that has interest,
or for a woman's marriage contract, because of food support!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in the story of step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: מרימר's ruling that a divorced woman collects from young orphans' property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רב אסי no interest is growing here; by רבי יוחנן the reason is food support, which a divorced woman doesn't get.

steps.title: Even רבי יוחנן only allows it for a widow
steps.stepSummary: רבינא sharpens his point: רבי יוחנן's rule is only for a widow, whose food costs the orphans money, not for a divorced woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יוחנן only said this about a widow, because her food support causes a loss. But a divorced woman, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes his challenge further. He says the ruling fails even according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow keeps eating from the estate until she is paid, so waiting hurts the orphans. A divorced woman is not fed from the estate, so there is no loss to the orphans if she waits. So the ruling fits neither opinion.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yochanan only said it
about a widow, who causes a loss through her food support,
but a divorced woman, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא בְּאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the challenge of step 35 stronger by applying it even to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: מרימר's ruling, even according to רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's reason, food support, only exists for a widow, not for a divorced woman.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason is חינא, which fits a divorced woman too
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that his tradition gives רבי יוחנן's reason as חינא: so the woman can remarry. That reason applies to a divorced woman as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned רבי יוחנן's statement with the reason 'because of favor.'
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רבינא's challenge. He says רבינא has the wrong reason for רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא thought the reason was the widow's food support. אמימר learned the reason is חינא: if she gets her money quickly, men will want to marry her. Every woman, widow or divorced, needs this, so the ruling fits רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: favor, so she will be seen well and can remarry
we learn it, we have the tradition

steps.whatToRemember: By אמימר's version of רבי יוחנן, a court collects a כתובה from young orphans for any woman, divorced or widowed, so she can remarry.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אֲנַן דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: He said to him: This statement of Rabbi Yochanan, we
learn it as being because of favor.
phrases.notes: Meaning: she should get her money quickly so men will want to marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֲנַן דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם חִינָּא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 35-36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the reason behind רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's reason is the widow's food support, so it only covers a widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's reason is חינא, so it covers a divorced woman too, and the ruling fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רב נחמן changes his practice about orphans' property
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he used to avoid dealing with orphans' property, but after hearing רב's saying that orphans who eat what isn't theirs should follow their parent, he began to deal with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: At first I would not deal with orphans' property. Once I heard what our friend רב הונא said in the name of רב: 'Orphans who eat what is not theirs, let them go after the ones who left them,' from then on I would deal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב נחמן about his own practice. He explains why he changed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first רב נחמן protected orphans by not collecting from their property. רב's sharp saying taught him that keeping money that belongs to someone else is very serious, even for orphans. So he started letting people collect from orphans' property.

keyTerms.meaning: I would deal with, get involved with
those who left them behind (their dead parent)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן ended up being willing to collect debts from orphans' property, because eating what isn't yours is very serious.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵרֵישָׁא לָא הֲוָה מִיזְדְּקִיקְנָא לְנִכְסֵי יַתְמֵי,
phrases.english: At first I would not deal with the property of orphans,
once I heard this
of Rav Huna, our friend, in the name of Rav:
"Orphans who eat what is not theirs,
let them go after those who left them,"
phrases.notes: Their dead parent. It's a sharp curse: they should follow him to the grave.

phrases.english: from then on I would deal with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מֵרֵישָׁא לָא הֲוָה מִיזְדְּקִיקְנָא לְנִכְסֵי יַתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כתובה question to a general statement about collecting from orphans' property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן changed his practice and began dealing with orphans' property so that people could collect what was owed to them.

steps.title: Why did רב נחמן hold back at first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's original practice of not collecting from orphans' property.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the beginning, what was the reason he did not collect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב נחמן's statement from the last step and asks why he originally refused to collect from orphans. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said he changed his practice, but he never told us why he held back in the first place. The גמרא wants that original reason, because it will decide which cases are affected.

phrases.english: At first, what is the reason he did not [collect]?
phrases.notes: This is about רב נחמן from the last step, who at first would not touch orphans' property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the earlier practice that רב נחמן described in Step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רב נחמן originally avoided collecting debts from orphans' property.

steps.title: Paying a debt is a מצוה, and young orphans are not obligated
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that repaying a creditor is a מצוה, and minor orphans are not obligated in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Paying back a creditor is a מצוה, and orphans are not people who are obligated to do מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first reason: paying a debt is a מצוה, and young orphans are not obligated in מצוות. So the court does not make them pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, the problem has nothing to do with any doubt about the debt. Even if the debt is certainly still owed, the orphans are simply not obligated in the מצוה of paying it. That makes it a very broad reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (here, young ones who are not yet adults)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Repaying a creditor is a מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: וְיַתְמֵי לָא בְּנֵי מֶיעְבַּד מִצְוָה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: and orphans are not obligated to perform a מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means orphans who are still minors. They are not yet obligated in מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרִיעַת בַּעַל חוֹב מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Repaying debts is a מצוה, and minor orphans are not obligated in מצוות, so the court does not collect from them.

steps.title: Maybe the father already paid
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a different reason: maybe the father already handed the creditor bundles of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Say that maybe he gave him bundles of coins.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives another reason. Maybe before he died, the father gave the creditor bundles of coins to cover the debt, and the young orphans would not know about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is based on doubt: maybe the debt was already paid. The court waits until the orphans grow up and can find out what happened. Unlike רב פפא's reason, this one only matters when there really is a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed it over to him (as payment or security)
Say that maybe; we worry that

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Say that he handed him bundles [of coins].
phrases.notes: The worry is that the father paid the creditor before he died, and the young orphans don't know it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר צְרָרֵי אַתְפְּסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing answer to the question in Step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court holds back because the father may have already paid, and the orphans cannot yet check.

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different results. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain why we do not collect from young orphans. The גמרא wants a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is [the difference] between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in Steps 40 and 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רב פפא's reason and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's reason would give different rulings.

steps.title: Cases where the debt is clearly still owed
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when the debtor admitted he owed the money, or when he was put in שמתא for not paying and died in that state.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when the one who owes admits it, or when they put him in שמתא and he died while still in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names cases where there is no doubt the debt is still owed. In those cases the two reasons give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the debtor admitted the debt, or died while in שמתא for not paying, we know he never paid. So רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's worry about secret payment is gone, and we collect. But for רב פפא the orphans are still not obligated in the מצוה, so we still do not collect.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who owes admits the debt
They put him in שמתא (a form of excommunication) to force him to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two reasons disagree on whether we collect in ordinary cases. In a normal case both say we wait. They only split when it is certain the debt was never paid.

phrases.english: There is [a difference] between them where the one obligated admits,
or also where they excommunicated him
phrases.notes: The court put the father in שמתא because he refused to pay. That shows he had not paid.

phrases.english: and he died in his excommunication.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ בְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 42 by naming the cases where the two reasons give different results.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the debt is certainly unpaid (the debtor admitted it, or he died in שמתא), רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע would collect, while רב פפא would not.

steps.title: Ruling from ארץ ישראל: we follow רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A message from ארץ ישראל says these collection cases are about a father who died in שמתא, and the הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: [It is a case] where they put him in שמתא and he died in his שמתא, and the הלכה is like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: Scholars in ארץ ישראל sent a message saying that the cases where we collect from orphans are cases where the father died in שמתא. They ruled like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting from young orphans when the father died in שמתא only works with רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's reason, because there is no doubt the debt is unpaid. Under רב פפא's reason we could never collect from minors. So the message settles the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there (from ארץ ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: We do not collect a debt from young orphans when there is a chance their father already paid. But if it is certain he never paid, as when he died in שמתא, we do collect, following רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: holding back from orphans is based on doubt about payment, not on orphans being free from the obligation.

phrases.english: They sent from there:
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: [It is] where they excommunicated him and he died in his excommunication,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: and the halakha is in accordance with Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the difference from Step 43 to decide between the two reasons.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: we collect from young orphans' property only when it is certain the debt was never paid, such as when the father died in שמתא.
